name: Round straw bale
notes:
A standard round field bale, and the reason it exists is docs/70: Robin's own example of an assembly absorbing an impact — *"we could have a rock fall on a haystack, unsettle the hay (dry grass), but the impact could be absorbed."*

NOTHING HERE IS CHOSEN. The dimensions are a standard round bale (1.2 m x 1.2 m). The PACKING is the measured bulk density of a field bale over straw's own cell-wall density: 100 / 1400 = 0.0714 — so the bale is 92.9% AIR, which is the whole point. That void is what an impact closes, and `compressive_strength` (45 kPa, mid-range of published straw-bale compression tests at 20% strain) is what closing it costs.

Mass follows: envelope 1.357 m3 x packing x 1400 kg/m3 = 136 kg, which is what a round bale weighs.

FLAGGED: one part, so it compacts uniformly. A real bale crushes locally under the strike and stays whole elsewhere; the honest version is the bale as a stack of parts, which is the same resolution question every assembly here faces.
